AR221
Archaeology of Greece and Rome
0.5 Credit
Hours per week:
Lecture/Discussion: 3
This
course
aims to provide
students
with a thorough introduction to the art and archaeology of the Greek and Roman world from the 15th century B.C. through the 4th century A.D. We will explore the development and transformation of political, economic, social, and religious institutions, in addition to assessing archaeological evidence for the daily life of all segments of the Greek and Roman population. Perceptions of Greek and Roman archaeology in modern culture and popular media will also be examined.
Additional Course Information
Exclusions
AR214, AR215, CL214, CL215.
